  "plain_name": "Missing ECDSA signature range check",
  "weakness": "When checking an ECDSA signature, the affected OpenJDK code does not first check that the signature's two numbers (r and s) are in the allowed range, meaning not zero and below a fixed limit that belongs to the curve. The fixed code refuses such a signature straight away by returning false; the affected code has no such step and goes on to calculate with the numbers.",
  "weakness_quote": {"source": "S4", "text": "if (rb.signum() == 0 || sb.signum() == 0"},
  "kind": "accepts_bad_signature",
  "area": "ecdsa_signature_check",
  "affected": {"versions": "OpenJDK 18, 17.0.2 and earlier in the 17 line, 15.0.6 and earlier in the 15 line", "quote": {"source": "S1", "text": "The affected versions are 18, 17.0.2, 15.0.6,"}},
  "fixed": {"version": "17.0.3", "quote": {"source": "S6", "text": "DEFAULT_VERSION_UPDATE=3"}},
  "notes": "17.0.3 is the fixed release of the 17 line only (the fixed source's version file reads feature 17, interim 0, update 3): 18 is listed as affected although its number is higher, and these sources do not name the fixed releases for the 15 and 18 lines. The OpenJDK sentence about affected versions covers every fix in that release and goes on to list 13.0.10, 11.0.14, 8u322 and 7u331; the table row for this CVE marks only columns 15, 17 and 18, so 7, 8, 11 and 13 are not marked for it, and lines with no column, such as 16, are not covered either way. Oracle's list names only versions it supported (Oracle Java SE 17.0.2 and 18; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition 21.3.1 and 22.0.0.2), so it does not mention the 15 line or earlier 17 releases, and Oracle changed that list on 2022-April-21, so an older copy may differ. No source gives an example of a signature that wrongly passes; the kind given here rests on the missing check (seen by comparing the 17.0.2 and 17.0.3 code) and on Oracle describing the effect as unauthorised changes to data."
